fredmd.nonidentified_tcode.spec: non-identified after applying each series' PUBLISHED McCracken-Ng transformation code; identical MCS protocol, alpha=0.10, only the stationarity transform differs. CAVEAT: part of the drop from fredmd.nonidentified_levels_subset is mechanical, not purely 'stationarity was an artifact' -- the tcode transform (e.g. log-difference) can turn a trending level series into a near-white-noise target, on which the `theta` model (in MODELS above) tends to degenerate toward a near-constant forecast; that alone can separate `theta` from the other three models on absolute loss and shrink |MCS|, independent of whether non-stationarity was inflating the levels-side count. Read this key beside fredmd.nonidentified_levels_subset as a bound, not a clean counterfactual

fredmd.spearman_gap_mcs.spec: Spearman rank correlation between the studentized best-vs-second-best gap and |MCS_abs| across the population panel

fredmd.squared_nonidentified.spec: series with |MCS_sq|>1 at alpha=0.10; identical protocol to fredmd.nonidentified, squared rather than absolute loss. NOTE: despite its name, this file's MCS_sq is a rooted RMSSE (sqrt per year, then pooled) and so matches mcs_test.py's 'MCS_rmsse', NOT mcs_test.py's own 'MCS_sq' column, which is deliberately un-rooted; a reader cross-referencing the two CSVs by column name alone would be misled about which construction this one uses. Not quoted in the manuscript (cites=[]).

fredmd.tcode_subset.spec: series carrying a PUBLISHED McCracken-Ng transformation code, on which the levels and transformed specifications are both defined and therefore comparable. Excludes any series whose transformed values are dominated by a near-zero-crossing arithmetic artifact (see tcode_outlier_ratio()) -- 1 series excluded this run on that basis
